slots.practicalActivity: Open a free public REST API in the browser (e.g. https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/posts/1) and in a terminal run the same request with curl. Identify, in writing, the resource, the HTTP method being used, and why this counts as a REST-style call.
slots.deliverable: A short note identifying the resource, method, and REST characteristics for 3 different real endpoint calls you made.

slots.practicalActivity: Using curl or Postman against https://httpbin.org, issue a GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, and DELETE request and record the real status code each one returns, including deliberately hitting a path that returns a 404.
slots.deliverable: A table of 5 real method-to-status-code pairs captured from actual requests.

slots.practicalActivity: Use curl -v (or your browser's Network tab) against a real API endpoint to capture the full raw request and response: request line, headers, body, status line, response headers, and response body.
slots.deliverable: An annotated capture of one real raw HTTP request and response, with each section (headers, body, status line) labeled.

slots.practicalActivity: Read Anthropic's real Messages API reference documentation and extract the base URL, the required authentication header, the required request fields, and the shape of a successful response.
slots.deliverable: A one-page notes file answering: base URL, auth header name, required params, and response field names, sourced directly from the real docs.

slots.practicalActivity: Chapter wrap lab: pick a public API you haven't used yet this chapter (e.g. the Open-Meteo weather API or PokeAPI), read its docs cold, and make one real GET request with the correct query parameters and headers.
slots.deliverable: A working script or curl command plus the real JSON response it returned, saved to a file.

slots.practicalActivity: Hand-write (don't generate) a nested JSON document representing a multi-turn chat conversation: a top-level array of {role, content} objects plus a nested metadata object with a model name and token counts.
slots.deliverable: A valid .json file, hand-written, verified by running it through json.loads() or a JSON linter without errors.

slots.practicalActivity: Write a JSON Schema that validates the parameters object for a tool-calling function like get_weather(location, unit), then construct one payload that passes validation and one that deliberately fails it.
slots.deliverable: A schema file plus two test payloads (valid and invalid), both actually run through a JSON Schema validator with the real pass/fail result recorded.

slots.practicalActivity: In Python, call json.loads() on a real API response, walk its nested keys safely using .get() instead of direct indexing, and add a handler for a missing or malformed field.
slots.deliverable: A working parsing script that handles at least one deliberately malformed input without crashing.

slots.practicalActivity: Debug 5 deliberately broken JSON snippets you write yourself (a trailing comma, single quotes instead of double, an unescaped newline in a string, a duplicate key, and a leading-zero number), fixing each one.
slots.deliverable: A before/after list of the 5 fixed JSON snippets with a one-line explanation of what was wrong with each.

slots.practicalActivity: Chapter wrap lab: create 5 small JSON files (a mix of 3 valid and 2 invalid against a schema you define), then write a Python script that validates each file against the schema and reports pass/fail per file.
slots.deliverable: A validation script plus its real pass/fail output report for all 5 files.

slots.practicalActivity: Compare the real request/response shape of an OpenAI-style chat completion request against Anthropic's Messages API request, side by side, noting field-name differences (messages/model/choices vs. model/messages/content).
slots.deliverable: A side-by-side comparison table of real field names between the two provider API shapes.

slots.practicalActivity: Write a Python script that opens a real streaming request (stream: true) to an AI provider's Messages API, reads the SSE events as they arrive, accumulates the text_delta chunks into one running string, and only prints the final string once message_stop arrives.
slots.deliverable: A working streaming script, run against a real API key, that prints the correctly accumulated final message.

slots.practicalActivity: Define a real tool schema (JSON) for a function such as get_stock_price(ticker), send a request including that tools parameter to an AI provider API, and inspect the tool-use block the model returns.
slots.deliverable: The tool schema JSON plus a captured real API response showing the model invoking that tool with specific arguments.

slots.practicalActivity: Deliberately trigger a real 401 (invalid API key) and a real 404 (bad endpoint path), then write exception handling that distinguishes retryable errors (429, 5xx) from non-retryable ones (4xx).
slots.deliverable: A script with try/except logic that handles at least 3 distinct real HTTP error codes with different, correct behavior for each.

slots.practicalActivity: Call a real paginated endpoint (e.g. GitHub's /users/{user}/repos, or a cursor-based list-models endpoint) and follow its real next-page cursor or link header across multiple requests until exhausted.
slots.deliverable: A script that collects every page into one combined list, with the real total item and page count printed.

slots.practicalActivity: Stand up a small local webhook receiver (Flask or Python's http.server) and send it a simulated POST payload shaped like a real provider webhook event, checking for a signature header the way a production receiver would.
slots.deliverable: A running local webhook endpoint plus a captured example payload it actually received and logged.

slots.practicalActivity: Chapter wrap lab: build one script that makes a real streaming request to an AI provider with a tool defined, handles a simulated rate-limit (429) with a retry/backoff loop, and logs every distinct SSE event type it receives.
slots.deliverable: One integrated script combining streaming, tool calling, and error handling, run successfully against a real API key.

slots.practicalActivity: Sketch and implement the skeleton of an AIClient class: __init__ storing api_key and base_url, and one placeholder method per real action (send_message, list_models), matching the real endpoints covered in Chapter 3.
slots.deliverable: A client class file with correct method signatures (no bodies yet) matching real provider API actions.

slots.practicalActivity: Implement the client's error handling: custom exception classes for distinct failure types, and a retry loop that only retries transient failures (429/5xx), never 4xx client errors.
slots.deliverable: An updated AIClient with custom exceptions and a working retry loop, demonstrated recovering from a forced transient failure.

slots.practicalActivity: Add real rate-limit header reading (e.g. retry-after, x-ratelimit-remaining) to the client, and implement exponential backoff with jitter for when those headers indicate a wait.
slots.deliverable: A client method that reads real rate-limit headers and backs off correctly, demonstrated against a mocked 429 response.

slots.practicalActivity: Write at least 3 unit tests using mocking (unittest.mock or the responses library) proving the retry loop recovers from a simulated 429 followed by success, and that a non-retryable 400 raises immediately without retrying.
slots.deliverable: A test file with 3 or more passing tests exercising both the retry path and the non-retryable error path.

lessons.title: Capstone: A Reusable AI API Client

slots.practicalActivity: Assemble the full AIClient class against the real requirements checklist: correct request/response handling, resilient error handling, rate-limit awareness, a tested retry path, and clean class design with one method per real action.
slots.deliverable: A completed AIClient.py satisfying all 5 checklist requirements, runnable end to end against a real API key.

slots.practicalActivity: Write a README documenting the AIClient's public methods and their arguments, then run it live against the real API one more time to capture one actual successful response as a demo for the README.
slots.deliverable: A README.md plus a captured real successful API call output, ready to drop into a portfolio repository.

monthlyMilestoneContribution: After finishing this course, a student can read any REST API's documentation cold, correctly produce and parse the JSON shapes AI provider APIs actually use (including streaming and tool calling), and has built and tested a real, reusable Python client class that talks to a live AI API with proper error handling and rate-limit backoff.
